grammar_focus: 复习 KS17/41/65 情态表达(收官包·干净课美语化):must(必须、务必;must have done 对过去的肯定推测)、have to / had to(客观上必须)、needn't 与 don't have to(不必)、should / should have done(应该/过去本应做)、mustn't(禁止)的用法与辨析
scene: “上台一定要沉住气,”老师叮嘱新来的主持人。“你不必做到完美,但要吐字清楚。”那天晚上,主持人要介绍一位著名作家。他太紧张了,一定是把名字说混了。“你不用担心,”作家轻声安慰道,“谁都会这样。”“我当时真该多练练的,”主持人事后说。“别太苛责自己了,”她笑着回答。“下次我一定记得先深呼吸,”他笑道。“你该为自己骄傲——你坚持下来了!”她说。大家都认同:一个小小的口误,不必毁掉一个愉快的夜晚。

grammar_card.title: 复习 KS17/41/65 情态表达
grammar_card.intro: 本课复习几个常用的情态说法:①must——主观上“必须、务必”(You must stay calm);must have done——对过去的肯定推测“一定……过了”(He must have mixed up the names);②have to / had to——客观上“不得不、必须”,过去用 had to(He had to introduce the writer);③needn't 和 don't have to——“不必、无需”(You needn't worry / You don't have to be perfect);④should——“应该”,should have done——“过去本应做而没做”(I should have practiced more);⑤mustn't——“禁止、别”(You mustn't be so hard on yourself)。

rows: You must stay calm. / He must have mixed up the names.
He had to introduce a famous writer.
You needn't worry. / You don't have to be perfect.
You should speak clearly. / I should have practiced more.
You mustn't be so hard on yourself.

specialRules.rule: 美语“剧院”说 theater(英式 theatre);“电梯”说 elevator(英式 lift)。本课已按美语写。
needn't / don't have to = 不必(没必要),mustn't = 禁止(一定别);must have done 是对过去的推测,should have done 是“本应做却没做”。

prelisten.q: Listen and answer — What did the teacher tell the new host to do?

passage: "You must stay calm on stage," the teacher told the new host. "You don't have to be perfect, but you should speak clearly." That evening, the host had to introduce a famous writer. He was so nervous that he must have mixed up the names. "You needn't worry," the writer whispered kindly. "It happens to everyone." "I should have practiced more," the host said afterward. "You mustn't be so hard on yourself," she replied with a smile. "Next time, I must remember to breathe first," he laughed. "You should be proud — you kept going!" she said. Everyone agreed: a small slip needn't ruin a good evening.

grammar_points.name: must(必须)与 must have done(对过去的推测)
have to / had to(客观上必须)
needn't 与 don't have to(不必)
should 与 should have done(应该/本应做)

stage5.stem: "'You ___ stay calm on stage,' the teacher said."(主观上“必须、务必”)
"He was so nervous that he ___ mixed up the names."(对过去的肯定推测:一定是)
stage5.stem_cn: 他太紧张了,一定是把名字说混了。

stage5.stem: "'Next time, I ___ remember to breathe first,' he laughed."(必须、一定要)
stage5.stem_cn: “下次我一定记得先深呼吸,”他笑道。

stage5.stem: "That evening, the host ___ introduce a famous writer."(过去客观上不得不)
stage5.stem_cn: 那天晚上,主持人要介绍一位著名作家。

stage5.stem: "Actors ___ practice a lot before a big show."(客观上必须)
stage5.stem_cn: 演员在大型演出前必须多加排练。

stage5.stem: "Yesterday she ___ leave early to catch a train."(过去客观上不得不)
stage5.stem_cn: 昨天她不得不早走去赶火车。

stage5.stem: "'You ___ be perfect,' the teacher said."(不必、没必要)
"'You ___ worry,' the writer whispered."(不必、无需)
"A small slip ___ ruin a good evening."(不必、无需)
stage5.stem_cn: 一个小口误不必毁掉一个愉快的夜晚。

stage5.stem: "'You ___ speak clearly,' the teacher said."(应该)
"'I ___ practiced more,' the host said afterward."(过去本应做却没做)
stage5.stem_cn: “我当时真该多练练的,”主持人事后说。

stage5.stem: "'You ___ be proud — you kept going!' she said."(应该)
stage5.stem_cn: “你该为自己骄傲——你坚持下来了!”她说。

stage5.stem: "'You ___ be so hard on yourself,' she replied."(表示“别、禁止这样”)
"He didn't prepare, so he ___ have mixed up the names."(对过去的肯定推测)
stage5.stem_cn: 他没准备,所以一定是把名字说混了。

stage5.stem: "There's no rule about it; you ___ come if you don't want to."(主观上不必)
stage5.stem_cn: 这事没规定,你要是不想来就不必来。

stage5.stem: "The new ___ welcomed everyone to the show."(主持人用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 新主持人欢迎大家来看演出。

stage5.stem: "He was very ___ before speaking to the crowd."(紧张的用哪个词)
stage5.stem_cn: 在对众人讲话前,他非常紧张。

stage5.stem: "'Try to stay ___,' the teacher said."(镇静的、冷静的用哪个词)
